strings.name: Venki Ramakrishnan
strings.role: Structural biologist · Participant in public science affairs
strings.summary: Ramakrishnan studied physics in India, earned a US doctorate and switched to biology before working on ribosomes at Cambridge’s LMB. His team resolved the small ribosomal subunit, advancing understanding of protein synthesis and antibiotic action. He shared the 2009 chemistry Nobel with Steitz and Yonath. Royal Society president from 2015 to 2020, he also wrote about research practice and the science of ageing.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Studied ribosome structure and function, advancing understanding of cellular protein synthesis while contributing to science policy and public communication.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu, India; born in 1952.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Ribosome structure
strings.highlights.h1.text: His team used structural methods to study the small subunit and antibiotic interactions, illuminating protein synthesis.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Physics BSc, Baroda (1971); physics PhD, Ohio University (1976); later studied biology at UC San Diego.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research and society
strings.highlights.h2.text: Served as Royal Society president and wrote about research and ageing, contributing to policy and public debate.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Why We Die published
strings.timeline.t1.text: Explained ageing and lifespan research while examining evidence and hype around life-extension ambitions.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Royal Society presidency ended
strings.timeline.t2.text: Completed the presidency begun in 2015 and continued research and public communication.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Royal Society president
strings.timeline.t3.text: Began leading the British scientific academy and engaging in research and public policy debate.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Shared chemistry Nobel
strings.timeline.t4.text: Shared the award with Thomas Steitz and Ada Yonath for studies of ribosome structure and function.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Small-subunit structure
strings.timeline.t5.text: His team published a high-resolution ribosomal small-subunit structure, advancing understanding of translation and antibiotic binding.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined Cambridge LMB
strings.timeline.t6.text: Moved from the United States to Britain and joined the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Physics doctorate and switch to biology
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned an Ohio physics PhD and subsequently trained in biology at San Diego.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Indian physics degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned a Baroda physics degree before further study in the United States.
